messages:
Eli Huang: @channel urgent escalation from customer 'EduPay' — they're seeing repeated 504s and request timeouts hitting our hosted inference endpoint (model: gptx-7b-proxy). Report started ~10:02 UTC. Customer says tail requests take >30s then 504. Logs show continuous batching backlog; queue depth at 100% and early-rejects disabled. Request IDs: rQ:0a3f2c, rQ:0a3f2d. Example client curl:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer/gptx-7b-proxy

Response stuck, then 504.

Support Bot: Customer ticket #INC-6942 created and linked. Notified account owner Frank (Acct). ETA for first response: 10:10 UTC. Included logs and sample requests.

Maria P.: Thanks Eli. Jumping in — first-pass triage: indicators of continuous batching backlog: runtime_batched_queue_depth avg: 128 (limit=128), batcher_pending_count spikes, kv-cache hit rate unchanged. Do we have autoscale activity?

Jon (SRE): Not seeing autoscale scale-up during the spike. GPU pool for hosted-region us-west2 is at 95% mem. Metrics: instance count unchanged, pending_queue_time p95 jumped from 40ms->1.2s. Looks like queue-depth enforcement prevented new workers because of shard placement delay.

Eli Huang: Customer load is a mix of short chat messages and some long context requests; continuous batching is grouping many short requests into large batches and backlog forms. Tail latency amplifies because of max_queue_depth=128 and batching window of 40ms.

Jon (SRE): Quick mitigation: enable early_reject_threshold=0.85 for that tenant (edu-pay-tenant) so we fail fast on overload rather than piling up. Also temporarily lower batching_max_window_ms to 15ms in the proxy routing config for that tenant. Will push a config patch to staging then prod.

OpsBot: Applied config change to routing/prod for tenant edu-pay-tenant: early_reject_threshold=0.85, batching_max_window_ms=15. Change id: cfg-2026-03-15-edu-1. Rollout started 10:16 UTC -> 10:18 UTC.

Support Bot: Customer notified of mitigation steps at 10:19 UTC. Asking them to repro and send latest request IDs.

Frank (Acct): FYI customer flagged this as impacting payments flow during peak hour — needs concrete SLA comment. Can we confirm whether this was tenant load-specific or global?

Maria P.: So far looked tenant-local: only edu-pay-tenant showed queue depth at limit; others normal. However, we're seeing an underlying scheduling lag in the batcher allocator when many ephemeral flows appear. This causes the pool to not spin up additional batcher workers fast enough. Root cause hypothesis: allocator timeouts under high ephemeral concurrency + zk-like leader contention in placement service.

Eli Huang: Repro steps I used in staging to reproduce the backlog: 
1) spin a 500rps client with 80% short 50-token requests and 20% 2000-token requests targeted to gptx-7b-proxy tenant routing. (script attached in thread).
2) observe batcher_pending_count and queued_requests. p95 latency >12s when queue depth limits reached.

Code snippet (loadgen):
```bash
# simplified repro loop
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/infer/gptx-7b-proxy \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":50}' &
  sleep 0.002
done
wait
```

Jon (SRE): Good repro. I also dumped the allocator logs and found repeated WARNs: "placement: worker-lease-acquire timeout (200ms)" and backoff cycles. That lines up with leader election/coordination slowness.

Maria P.: Immediate follow-ups: 
- (P0) Keep early_reject in place for edu-pay and watch 5xx rate; rollback if false positives.
- (P1) Increase max_queue_depth for hosted pools from 128->192 only if batcher worker scaling is fixed (risk: longer tails).
- (P1) Reduce batching_max_window_ms globally from 40->25ms as a safe compromise — schedule for gradual rollout.
- (P2) Hotfix allocator timeouts to avoid slow lease acquisition: bump timeout to 400ms and instrument leader metrics.

Eli Huang: Customer confirmed reduced 504s after early_reject change; they still see occasional 5s tail requests. Support asked for timeline to avoid recurrence.

Jon (SRE): I'll create a short-lived autoscale override to add +2 batcher instances to us-west2 for 2h to absorb peak while we fix allocator. Pushing as manual scaling action at 10:32 UTC.

OpsBot: Manual scale applied: +2 batcher nodes to pool us-west2. pool-change-id: pool-1102-boost.

Maria P.: Logging action items here and opening a post-incident Jira: REDWOOD-INC-3259. Draft incident notes: cause = allocator lease acquisition/backoff under ephemeral concurrency -> queue depth hit -> continuous batching backlog -> tail-timeouts and 504s.

Jon (SRE): Long-term mitigations we should own: 
- better leader election backoff routines and faster lease handoff (allocator rewrite)
- adaptive batching: if queue depth rising fast, reduce window per-tenant automatically
- tenant-level throttling knobs surfaced in Console for enterprise admins
- better pre-warming heuristics for ephemeral high-concurrency flows

Eli Huang: Quick TODOs for next 24h: 
- validate early_reject didn't create user-visible false rejects (Maria)
- roll out allocator timeout bump to staging + canary (Jon)
- schedule batcher autoscale policy change (Ops)
- account outreach + RCA draft to EduPay (Frank + Support)

Support Bot: Noted. Ticket updated with mitigation timeline and next update ETA 14:00 UTC.

Frank (Acct): Please include cost impact if we keep higher pool capacity; customer will want options: dedicated reserved capacity vs burst credits.

Maria P.: I'll run a quick cost vs tail-latency tradeoff calc and paste numbers in the ticket. Early estimate: +2 nodes during peak ~ $1.8k/day; Dedicated reserved could eliminate noisy neighbors but needs contract.

Eli Huang: Will keep monitoring. If anyone sees a re-escalation, @Jon (SRE) please reopen. Closing thread after postmortem and RCA published. :thumbsup:
